html:
In 1409 the Tibetan teacher Tsongkhapa founded Ganden Monastery on a mountain east of Lhasa. It became the mother house of the Gelug school, the youngest of the main traditions of Tibetan Buddhism.

Tsongkhapa stressed strict monastic rules, celibacy and long years of study and debate. His followers soon built two more great monasteries near Lhasa, Drepung and Sera. Together with Ganden they became huge monastic universities.

The Gelug school rose fast. Its leaders received the title of Dalai Lama from a Mongol khan in 1578, and with Mongol help the school took political power over Tibet in 1642 through the Ganden Phodrang government. Ganden itself was wrecked after 1959 and has since been partly rebuilt.
sum: In 1409 the Tibetan teacher Tsongkhapa founded Ganden Monastery on a mountain east of Lhasa. It became the mother house of the Gelug school, the youngest of the main traditions of Tibetan Buddhism.
